signals.topic: IntelliJ/JetBrains: file search returns unbounded results causing context window overflow in large repos
signals.summary: The IntelliJ implementation of getFileResults ignores the maxResults parameter, returning all matching files (10k+) on broad glob patterns. This immediately exhausts the context window and produces 400 errors in large repositories, making codebase search completely unusable in IntelliJ.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断+高频（2个相关issue指向同一根因）。IntelliJ用户在大仓库中使用@codebase时完全无法工作，返回大量无关文件导致 LLM 直接报 400 错误。属于关键上下文功能不可用。

source_issues.title: [Bug] Missing results limitation in IntelliJ getFileResults implementation causing context overflow
source_issues.evidence: IntelliJ returns entire file list on glob search without maxResults limit. Tested on 10k+ file repo. Results in immediate context window exhaustion and 400 Bad Request.

source_issues.title: [Bug] IntelliJ file search results exceed limits and cause token overflow
source_issues.evidence: Separate report confirming the same issue: file search in IntelliJ returns too many files, causing token limit errors. VS Code correctly enforces maxResults but IntelliJ does not.

signals.topic: Credits balance not recognized despite user having active credits — blocks all usage
signals.summary: Users with active paid credits ($54 confirmed in one case) are shown 'insufficient credits' errors, preventing any use of the Continue extension entirely. This is a critical account credit recognition failure.
aliases: insufficient credits error with active balance
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断。用户已付费但系统不认可其额度，导致插件完全无法使用。属于关键功能不可用，是最高级别的用户体验失败。

source_issues.title: You don't have enough credits? seriously
source_issues.evidence: User has $54 of credits confirmed but extension still prompts to buy more. Fresh install. No way to resolve without intervention.

signals.topic: maxTokens 配置接近 32k 时静默失败返回零 token，伴随事件监听器泄漏
signals.summary: 当 defaultCompletionOptions.maxTokens 设置为接近 32768 时（如 32256、32767、32768），Continue 返回 Result: Success 但 Generated Tokens: 0。配置合法值时正常工作，但边界值静默失败无报错。同时观察到潜在的事件监听器泄漏（571个监听器），导致内存增长和功能异常。
signals.review_reason: 静默失败：用户配置了合法参数但得到零输出，没有任何错误提示，用户以为成功了但实际没有。这导致用户工作被吞没，同时监听器泄漏造成内存泄漏，属于明显的功能异常和资源泄漏问题。

source_issues.title: Continue extension fails or returns zero tokens when defaultCompletionOptions.maxTokens is set near 32k and suggestion
source_issues.evidence: maxTokens 32256/32767/32768 produce 'Result: Success' but 'Generated Tokens: 0'. Internal buffer or validation boundary issue near 32k. Listener leak (571 listeners) also observed causing memory growth and silent failures.

signals.topic: v1.11.1 regression: tool error handling and name collision resolution broken after cleanup commit bb9bcd6 removed _extract_tool_name()
signals.summary: A cleanup commit removed the _extract_tool_name() method (previously added in PR #4656) as 'unused', causing tool error injection and name collision resolution to silently break in v1.11.1. This leads to tools with duplicate names not being distinguished, errors not captured as observations, and dependent features (result_as_answer, usage limits, caching) malfunctioning.
aliases: name collision resolution broken after cleanup refactor
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed regression introduced in v1.11.1 with a clearly identified root cause commit (bb9bcd6). It breaks core tool execution functionality (error handling, name collision resolution) that was fixed in PR #4656 just weeks earlier. Though count=1, the severity is elevated because it represents a regression from a working fix, directly impacting multi-tool workflows.

source_issues.title: Regression: PR #4656 fix broken in v1.11.1 - Tool error handling and name collision resolution
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: v1.10.1 works, v1.11.1 broken. Root cause identified as commit bb9bcd6 removing _extract_tool_name(). Impact: tool name collision resolution fails, error injection as observations fails, result_as_answer/usage limits/caching features break.

signals.topic: Async workflow blocks event loop with synchronous LLM calls in converter module when using akickoff()
signals.summary: When using akickoff() (async workflow), the converter module makes synchronous self.llm.call() which blocks the event loop. This prevents true async execution and causes hangs or deadlocks when output_json or output_pydantic are used on Tasks in async workflows.
aliases: sync llm call in async context
converter uses sync call in async workflow
signals.review_reason: Blocking the event loop in async workflows is a primary-flow阻断 issue. When users invoke async crews with akickoff() and use output_json or output_pydantic, the entire event loop blocks, defeating the purpose of async. This is a clear main-flow阻断 with well-documented code paths and reproducible steps.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Do not invoke synchronous call() on LLM from asynchronous workflow in _export_output / converter
source_issues.evidence: Code paths traced: task.py lines 605, 1258 invoke _export_output which delegates to converter module. Converter makes synchronous llm.call() calls blocking the event loop. Reproduction steps provided using self_evaluation_loop_flow example with akickoff(). Expected behavior: only await llm.acall() should be made from async workflows.

signals.topic: InternalInstructor silently discards base_url for OpenAI-compatible providers, routing structured output requests to api.openai.com instead of configured endpoint
signals.summary: When using vLLM, Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible provider with a custom base_url, the InternalInstructor class discards the base_url and sends all structured output requests (output_json/output_pydantic) to api.openai.com, causing ConnectTimeout or ConverterError failures. The bug is in _create_instructor_client() which only extracts model and provider but never forwards base_url.
aliases: instructor client wrong endpoint for OpenAI-compatible providers
structured output broken with custom base_url
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow阻断 bug: structured output (output_json/output_pydantic) silently fails for any OpenAI-compatible provider (vLLM, Ollama, etc.) with a custom base_url, routing to wrong endpoint. The bug is confirmed through code tracing, with clear evidence that main LLM calls work but converter path breaks. All structured-output-dependent workflows are blocked.

source_issues.title: [BUG] InternalInstructor discards base_url when creating instructor client — breaks OpenAI-compatible endpoints
source_issues.evidence: Full root cause analysis provided: internal_instructor.py _create_instructor_client() only extracts model_string and provider, never forwarding base_url. _get_llm_extra_kwargs() exists but is guarded by is_litellm=True, so non-LiteLLM OpenAI-compatible providers are affected. Result: ConnectTimeout/ConverterError in environments that cannot reach api.openai.com. Affects vLLM, Ollama, Azure OpenAI with custom endpoints, and any self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

signals.topic: KeyError crash in _handle_non_streaming_response when response_model is used without 'messages' key in params
signals.summary: In llm.py, both _handle_non_streaming_response() and _ahandle_non_streaming_response() first validate that 'messages' key exists (raising ValueError), but then immediately access params['messages'] directly instead of the already-validated messages variable, causing KeyError for callers using response_model.
aliases: structured output KeyError in llm handler
signals.review_reason: This is a crash bug (KeyError) that occurs in a specific but valid code path: using response_model without the 'messages' key in params. The bug was identified through code review with precise line-level analysis. While it requires a specific calling pattern, it causes a direct crash with a confusing KeyError message instead of a helpful error, making debugging difficult for affected users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] KeyError when params missing 'messages' key in _handle_non_streaming_response
source_issues.evidence: Code trace: _handle_non_streaming_response() at line 1220 and _ahandle_non_streaming_response() at line 1364 access params['messages'] directly despite having extracted messages via params.get('messages', []) earlier. When 'messages' key is absent from params, the first ValueError is raised but then the code continues and crashes with KeyError. Simple one-line fix identified: use already-validated messages variable instead of params['messages'].

signals.topic: MCPToolResolver silently returns empty tool list when MCP server returns no tools, causing UnboundLocalError crash
signals.summary: MCPToolResolver._resolve_native() silently returns an empty list when an MCP server returns no tools or when tool_filter removes all tools. This triggers an UnboundLocalError crash at tool_resolver.py line 412 because tools_list is never assigned. No warning is logged, making diagnosis extremely difficult for users whose MCP servers (Stdio/HTTP/SSE) appear to not provide tools.
aliases: MCP tool resolver crash empty tools
MCP server returning no tools causes crash
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed crash (UnboundLocalError) with a full stack trace. The bug occurs whenever an MCP server returns zero tools (a valid and common scenario), making it a reliable blocker for MCP integration users. The silent failure with no diagnostic output compounds the issue — users cannot understand why their MCP server tools are unavailable.

source_issues.title: [BUG] MCPToolResolver does not log warning when native MCP config returns no tools
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided: UnboundLocalError at tool_resolver.py line 412 in _resolve_native. The methods _resolve_native() silently returns empty tools_list while _resolve_external() properly logs a warning. Reproduction: configure agent with MCP server (Stdio/HTTP/SSE) that has no tools or uses tool_filter that returns nothing. Exact fix suggested: add warning log before returning empty list, matching behavior of external resolver path.

signals.topic: HTTP 429 rate limit errors cause CLI crashes and unhandled promise rejections, blocking user workflows
signals.summary: Users hitting 429 Too Many Requests on cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com experience unhandled promise rejections, CRITICAL unhandled errors, and broken IDE connections. Multiple users across different auth types are affected.
signals.review_reason: Two separate users hit 429 errors that result in CLI crashes and unhandled promise rejections. One user specifically notes CRITICAL: Unhandled Promise Rejection when encountering 429 during plan mode. This blocks the primary workflow (plan mode editing) and causes an unhandled exception, which is a clear user-impacting failure.

source_issues.title: status 429
source_issues.evidence: HTTP 429 on cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com streamGenerateContent endpoint causes: CRITICAL unhandled promise rejection, MCP error -32001 timeout, broken IDE connection. Full CLI workflow interrupted.

source_issues.title: 429 Error for Google AI Pro account - requesting help
source_issues.evidence: 429 errors on Google AI Pro account, model no longer appears in /stats session. User lost quota visibility and workflow is blocked.

signals.topic: Session resume leaves storage paths (plan/tracker/task) bound to startup session ID, causing workflow state inconsistency
signals.summary: When resuming a session, Storage retains the startup session ID while Config updates to the resumed session ID, causing plan files, tracker state, and task artifacts to be written to the wrong session namespace. Users see resumed chat working while plan/tracker data appears lost.
signals.review_reason: This is a real workflow-blocking bug: resumed sessions have split state where the conversation uses the resumed session ID but plan/tracker/task storage continues using the startup session ID. Users lose access to their plan mode files, tracker continuity breaks, and artifacts get orphaned. While count=1, the technical root cause is well-documented and the user impact (inconsistent resumed state) is severe enough to warrant P1.

source_issues.title: Resuming a session keeps plans/tracker/tasks bound to the startup session ID
source_issues.evidence: Storage.sessionId is captured readonly at construction time; Config.setSessionId() only updates config state, not already-constructed Storage. Plan/tracker/task dirs derive from Storage's captured ID, not the resumed session ID. User sees resumed chat but plan/tracker state drifts to startup session namespace.

signals.topic: CLI hard crashes when user pastes large chat history (18+ lines of console logs)
signals.summary: Pasting moderately-sized content (18 lines of Chrome console logs) causes the entire CLI to crash. User must use CTRL-C to terminate. The command line remains active but the CLI only pretends to process commands.
signals.review_reason: A hard crash that completely blocks user work is a critical failure. The user describes the CLI becoming unresponsive after a moderate-size paste, requiring CTRL-C to terminate. This is not a graceful error - it is a crash that requires process termination. The CLI then enters a zombie state. This is clearly a P1 user pain point.

source_issues.title: CLI Hard Crash
source_issues.evidence: Pasting 18 lines of Chrome console log messages causes entire CLI to crash. User cannot exit normally, must use CTRL-C. CLI then pretends to accept commands but does not respond. Main workflow is completely blocked.

signals.topic: Search text tool generates untruncated massive output, flooding terminal with content
signals.summary: The search text tool does not truncate or clip output by default, producing huge amounts of content that floods the terminal. Labeled P1 by maintainers. User experience severely degraded.
aliases: Tool output too verbose in compact mode
signals.review_reason: Explicitly labeled P1 by maintainers. The search tool produces unbounded output that floods the terminal, making the tool practically unusable. This is a clear experience degradation that prevents productive use of the search functionality.

source_issues.title: Search text tool can generate large amounts of output [standard/compact formats]
source_issues.evidence: Search text tool output is not truncated/clipped by default. Screenshot shows terminal flooded with content. Issue is labeled priority/p1 by maintainers. User in compact mode still receives unmanageable volume of output.

signals.topic: Gemini CLI binary not found when NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX is set to custom path, blocking installation
signals.summary: When NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX is set to $HOME/.local/, the globally installed gemini binary is not found, resulting in 'gemini: No such file or directory'. This prevents users from running the CLI entirely.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear installation failure that prevents the CLI from running entirely. While count=1 and single-repo, the user cannot execute the tool at all - this is a blocking issue for users with NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX configured. Worth noting as P2 since it's a specific environment constraint rather than a broad failure.

source_issues.title: `/usr/bin/gemini: No such file or directory` when NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX is set to $HOME/.local/$
source_issues.evidence: User has NPM_CONFIG_PREFIX=$HOME/.local/ set in bashrc. After npm install -g @google/gemini-cli, running 'gemini' yields '/usr/bin/gemini: No such file or directory'. CLI cannot be launched at all.

signals.topic: SSRF vulnerability in AgentAudio and VisitTool due to missing URL validation
signals.summary: User-controlled URLs in AgentAudio and VisitTool are passed to requests.get() without any validation, allowing access to internal network resources, cloud metadata endpoints, and internal services.
signals.review_reason: SSRF vulnerability in AgentAudio and VisitTool allows attackers to make outbound requests to internal/cloud metadata endpoints when smolagents processes untrusted URLs. While no CVE or in-wild exploitation is documented, SSRF in agent frameworks is a high-severity issue because agents routinely handle user-supplied URLs. The vulnerability is clearly described with specific file/line references and a recommended fix. This constitutes a real security boundary issue with potential for significant data exposure (e.g., cloud IMDS tokens) if smolagents processes attacker-controlled URLs.

source_issues.title: [Security] SSRF Vulnerability in AgentAudio and VisitTool - Server-Side Request Forgery
source_issues.evidence: User-controlled URLs in AgentAudio (agent_types.py:229) and VisitTool (default_tools.py:491) passed to requests.get() without validation. Impact listed as access to internal network, cloud metadata endpoints.

signals.topic: Serialization error messages display literal '{e}' instead of actual exception details
signals.summary: In ToolSerializer.dumps, a double-brace f-string bug causes the literal text '{e}' to appear in error messages instead of the actual exception, making serialization failures undebuggable.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug: f-string double-brace escape causes literal '{e}' in error output instead of the actual exception message. This directly impacts users by making all serialization failures (pickle errors, unsupported types, etc.) undebuggable. Users cannot diagnose why their tools or agents fail to serialize, blocking workflows that depend on agent persistence. Severity is reduced to P2 because it is a single occurrence and the underlying serialization mechanism still works — only the error message is degraded.

source_issues.title: BUG: f-string escape error in ToolSerializer.dumps causes uninformative error message
source_issues.evidence: Line 429 in serialization.py uses '{{e}}' which outputs literal '{e}' instead of the exception variable. Users see 'Cannot serialize object: {e}' with no actual exception details. Line 292 in the same file has the correct single-brace form.

signals.topic: Agent save/reload loses custom step_callbacks and final_answer_checks
signals.summary: When a MultiStepAgent is saved via save() and reloaded via from_folder(), custom step_callbacks and final_answer_checks are silently lost because these callable objects are explicitly ignored in to_dict().
signals.review_reason: Agent persistence loses user-registered step_callbacks and final_answer_checks silently. Users who save/reload pre-configured agents with monitoring or validation callbacks lose that configuration entirely, with no error or warning. This disrupts workflows that depend on agent state persistence for checkpointing, resumption, or deployment. Marked as P2 due to single-issue count and non-blocking nature (workaround of manual re-registration exists).

source_issues.title: feat: support serialization for step_callbacks and final_answer_checks in MultiStepAgent
source_issues.evidence: step_callbacks and final_answer_checks are callable objects explicitly ignored in to_dict(). When agent is saved and reloaded via from_folder(), custom callbacks are silently lost. Users must manually re-register callbacks after reload.

signals.topic: Autonomous agent 误将随机 seed 变更识别为有效改进，导致实验选择质量下降
signals.summary: 用户发现 autorewrite 流程将 mere seed 变更误报为有效实验改进（improve step），认为这类 'lucky gain' 会误导 agent 继续沿错误方向探索。问题源于评估指标（bpb）本身具有随机性，seed 变化产生的波动被算法错误归类为真实收益。
aliases: random seed registered as valid improvement
signals.review_reason: 用户在真实使用中观察到 seed 变更被系统识别为有效改进步骤（valid improve step），并明确指出这会误导 agent 重新尝试已证明有效的配置，浪费实验资源并可能将探索方向引向局部最优。这是核心工作流的算法可信度问题，直接影响 autonomous 实验选择质量。count=1 低于 P0 阈值，归为 P1。

source_issues.title: change of seed registered as improvement?
source_issues.evidence: 用户在真实使用中观察到 README 图表最后一个 step 是 seed 变更被识别为 valid step 降低 loss，但认为这只是随机幸运，质疑系统将 lucky gain 与真实改进混为一谈，直接损害了 agent 的实验选择质量。

signals.topic: GitHub Actions Copilot code review workflow 在清理 artifact 时因 token 权限不足返回 403 导致 workflow 阻断
signals.summary: Copilot code review workflow 中的 cleanup artifacts 步骤因 gh token 权限不足（403 Resource not accessible by integration）而失败，导致整个 workflow 进入 fail-fast 状态，无法正常完成。
signals.review_reason: workflow 明确因 403 权限错误在 artifact deletion 步骤阻断，process completed with exit code 1，提供了具体 run ID 和 job URL 作为可验证证据。虽为基础设施层面问题但直接导致 workflow 无法完成，cleanup job fail-fast 是明确的用户影响（workflow 阻断）。count=1 且为单仓问题，不满足 P0 要求，归为 P1。

source_issues.title: Copilot code review cleanup job fails deleting artifacts with 403
source_issues.evidence: issue 提供了具体失败 run ID（23775280758）、具体 job URL 和 403 错误信息，workflow 在 artifact deletion 步骤 fail-fast，导致 Copilot code review workflow 无法正常完成，cleanup 步骤完全阻断。

signals.topic: MCP servers listed twice in approval prompt when both .mcp.json and .deepagents/.mcp.json exist
signals.summary: When a project contains both a root .mcp.json and a .deepagents/.mcp.json with overlapping server entries (common with tools like rulesync that generate .deepagents/.mcp.json), each shared server appears twice in the startup approval prompt. This creates a confusing UX where users must approve the same server twice.
signals.review_reason: Confusing UX that causes double-approval prompts for the same MCP server. Not flow-blocking but creates friction for users who use common tools like rulesync that generate overlapping MCP configs. Count=2 confirms this is a recurring user scenario.

source_issues.title: MCP servers duplicated in approval prompt when both `.mcp.json` and `.deepagents/.mcp.json` exist
source_issues.evidence: User has two config files both containing the same MCP servers (root .mcp.json + rulesync-generated .deepagents/.mcp.json). deepagents reads both without deduplication, causing each server to appear twice in the approval prompt.

source_issues.title: MCP servers appear twice in approval prompt when both `.mcp.json` and `.deepagents/.mcp.json` exist
source_issues.evidence: Same issue as #2374 (closed as dup). Root cause is lack of deduplication when reading multiple MCP config files.

signals.topic: SKILL.md files over ~200 lines are truncated by read_file, causing skills to execute incorrectly
signals.summary: When a SKILL.md file exceeds approximately 200 lines (or 100 lines on some models), the read_file tool truncates the content and the skill executes with an incomplete/invalid structure. This causes silent wrong behavior — the skill starts executing without having read its full definition.
aliases: read_file offset limit on skill files
signals.review_reason: Core workflow is broken for any skill with >200 lines. The skill executes with an incomplete definition, leading to wrong behavior that is hard to debug since the file read silently succeeds. This blocks the skill feature for a common use case (long skill files).

source_issues.title: skills can not proper work: read_file for SKILL.md not read fully before execute it
source_issues.evidence: User reports skill with >200 lines executes wrong because read_file only reads the beginning part and starts execution before the full file is processed. Reproducible on gpt-5.4-mini, gpt-5.4, and gemma4. Skill structure is invalid at execution time due to truncation.

signals.topic: Default deepagents middleware stack silently suppresses Gemma 4 26B reasoning output with Ollama
signals.summary: When using gemma4:26b via Ollama with deepagents' default stack (specifically TodoListMiddleware + large BASE_AGENT_PROMPT), the model's reasoning output disappears entirely from streamed chunks. The same model works correctly when used directly via ChatOllama. This is a regression that breaks the core differentiator of reasoning models without any error message.
signals.review_reason: A key model feature (reasoning) is silently broken when using a popular Ollama model with deepagents' default configuration. The user has no error message to diagnose from and no easy opt-out from the breaking middleware. This represents a significant behavior change in a core feature.

source_issues.title: Bug: default deepagents stack suppresses Gemma 4 26B reasoning output with Ollama
source_issues.evidence: Bisected to deepagents' TodoListMiddleware combined with the large BASE_AGENT_PROMPT causing gemma4:26b reasoning tokens to drop to zero. No workaround available — user cannot opt out of TodoListMiddleware in the default stack. Model emits no error, silently loses its core capability.

signals.topic: read_file on PDF/binary files crashes with Bedrock Converse API due to missing document.name parameter
signals.summary: When FilesystemMiddleware reads a PDF or binary file via the read_file tool, it returns a file content block without a name field. The Bedrock Converse API requires a name field for document blocks, causing the agent to crash with a ParamValidationError when processing the tool result. The agent cannot handle PDF files at all on Bedrock.
signals.review_reason: A specific but valid use case (reading PDF files with Bedrock) causes a complete request failure with a ParamValidationError. The crash is silent and not recoverable from the agent's perspective — file reading on Bedrock is completely broken for non-trivial files.

signals.topic: ExperimentalMarkdownSyntaxTextSplitter O(n²) performance from list.pop(0) causing multi-second delays on large files

signals.review_reason: Measurable performance damage: 50k+ line documents take several seconds instead of milliseconds. Root cause is algorithmic (O(n²) vs O(n)), fix is trivial (deque). Significant degradation in production document processing pipelines.

source_issues.title: bug(text-splitters): ExperimentalMarkdownSyntaxTextSplitter has O(n²) performance due to list.pop(0)
source_issues.evidence: User measured 50k line markdown taking 'several seconds' instead of expected milliseconds. Root cause is list.pop(0) being O(n) per call in a while loop. Fix identified as collections.deque.popleft() which is O(1).

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor runs LLM-generated code with full host privileges and no sandbox isolation
signals.summary: The LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it via subprocess with full filesystem, network, and process access. There is no lightweight sandbox between 'completely unsandboxed' and 'full Docker container'. This exposes users to privilege escalation risk from indirect prompt injection or malicious code generation, with the only safeguard being a suppressible UserWarning.
aliases: LLM-generated code execution without privilege confinement
signals.review_reason: Issue #7475 documents a real architectural gap: LLM-generated code runs unsandboxed with full host privileges via LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor. The attack surface (prompt injection leading to privilege escalation) is specific and realistic. However, confidence is capped at 0.6 because there is no evidence of multiple users hitting this issue — it is a proposal framed issue, not a bug report from multiple affected users. P2 is appropriate given count=1 and the theoretical (vs. reported) nature of the impact.

source_issues.title: Add lightweight OS-level sandboxing via sandlock for LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor
source_issues.evidence: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code with full host privileges; only safeguard is a suppressible UserWarning. Attack scenario documented: indirect prompt injection causing generation of malicious code (exfiltrating SSH keys, installing backdoors) running with full filesystem/network/process access.

signals.topic: MCP server integrations lack fail-closed defaults — untrusted servers can execute tools without explicit opt-in
signals.summary: AutoGen's MCP server integrations accept connections from untrusted servers by default. Safety relies on user discipline and documentation warnings rather than hard runtime contracts. This creates a tool poisoning blast radius for users connecting to external MCP servers.
aliases: MCP tool integrations have no trust enforcement defaults
MCP server connections accepted without explicit trust policy
signals.review_reason: Issue #7266 identifies that MCP server integrations have no fail-closed defaults — untrusted servers are accepted silently unless the user explicitly configures trust policy. This is a specific trust boundary gap with documented acceptance criteria and affected codepaths. Confidence is 0.6 because this is a proposal/feature request rather than a bug report with multiple user reports of actual tool poisoning incidents. P2 is appropriate given count=1 and the proposal framing.

source_issues.title: Enforce fail-closed defaults for untrusted MCP server integrations
source_issues.evidence: README warns to only connect to trusted MCP servers, but runtime contracts do not enforce this by default. Safety relies on user discipline rather than hard fail-closed defaults. Untrusted MCP configurations are accepted silently unless user explicitly configures trust/policy.

signals.topic: MCP tool inputSchema $schema field causes all Anthropic tool calls to fail
signals.summary: Playwright MCP server's toMcpTool includes a top-level $schema field in inputSchema (from Zod v4 toJSONSchema), which violates MCP protocol spec and causes Anthropic API to reject ALL tool calls with a 400 error. One bad tool schema breaks the entire session.
aliases: MCP tool schema invalid for Claude Code/Desktop
signals.review_reason: MCP is a first-class Playwright feature. The $schema field from Zod v4 causes complete failure of all MCP tool calls when forwarded to Anthropic API — a critical regression for AI agent workflows. One bad schema breaks ALL tool calls in the session, making the feature entirely unusable for Claude Code/Desktop users.

source_issues.title: MCP: tool inputSchema includes $schema field, causing Anthropic API 400 errors
source_issues.evidence: Anthropic API returns 400 error for ALL tool calls once one invalid schema is present. Users of Claude Code, Claude Desktop, and mcp-remote are blocked from using Playwright MCP at all.

signals.topic: IPv6 address resolution failure blocks browser install in GitHub Actions CI
signals.summary: GitHub Actions runners have problematic IPv6 routing. When upgrading Playwright from 1.55 to 1.59, browser download fails with EADDRNOTAVAIL because the runner's IPv6 stack is broken but Playwright tries IPv6 addresses first.
aliases: Browser install fails in GitHub Actions due to IPv6
EADDRNOTAVAIL on browser download in CI
signals.review_reason: Browser install failure is a main-flow blocker. CI pipelines cannot run tests at all when browser download fails. This is a direct and documented CI failure on GitHub Actions, a primary CI platform for Playwright users.

source_issues.title: [Feature]: IPV6 disabling
source_issues.evidence: Playwright browser install fails with 'connect EADDRNOTAVAIL 2a00:1450:4007:80f::201b:443' — IPv6 address error on GitHub Actions. The error blocks the entire CI pipeline because Playwright cannot install browsers.

signals.topic: Codegen Inspector window does not open on Windows in v1.59.0
signals.summary: Regression introduced in 1.59.0: on Windows, running 'npx playwright codegen' opens the browser but the Playwright Inspector window never appears, making codegen completely non-functional on Windows.
signals.review_reason: Codegen is a flagship Playwright feature for test generation. The Inspector window not opening on Windows makes the entire codegen workflow non-functional, which is a critical regression for a core feature. Affects all Windows users upgrading to 1.59.0.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: Codegen and UI mode doesn't open on Windows
source_issues.evidence: Regression in v1.59.0 on Windows 11: browser window opens but Inspector panel is completely missing. Codegen is the primary UI for generating test scripts — this blocks the entire workflow for Windows users. Workaround is to downgrade to 1.58.2.

signals.topic: Docker image tag mismatch: v1.58.0-noble runs Playwright v1.59.0, causing version mismatch errors in CI
signals.summary: The Playwright Docker image with tag v1.58.0 actually contains Playwright v1.59.0, causing 'version mismatch' errors when the local client is still at v1.58. This breaks existing CI pipelines that pin a specific Docker image version.
aliases: Docker image version mismatch breaks CI
Playwright Docker image content doesn't match tag
signals.review_reason: CI pipeline failure is a direct, measurable cost impact. Pipelines that pinned the v1.58.0-noble image unexpectedly fail because the image contains a different Playwright version. This breaks existing reproducible CI setups, a primary use case for Docker images.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Docker image mcr.microsoft.com/playwright:v1.58.0-noble runs 1.59.0
source_issues.evidence: CI pipeline was passing with v1.58.0-noble image, then failed without any code changes due to version mismatch: server v1.59 vs client v1.58. The Docker image content does not match its tag, breaking existing CI pipelines.

signals.topic: WebKit locator.fill() silently fails on contenteditable elements inside shadow DOM in v1.59.0
signals.summary: Regression from 1.58.2 to 1.59.0: locator.fill() on contenteditable elements inside shadow DOM silently produces empty text on WebKit. The operation reports success but the content is never written, causing test assertions to fail silently.
aliases: WebKit contenteditable shadow DOM fill regression 1.59
locator.fill silently fails WebKit shadow DOM
signals.review_reason: locator.fill() is one of the most fundamental Playwright operations. Silent failure — where the action reports success but content is empty — is particularly dangerous as tests pass incorrectly. This regression specifically breaks WebKit tests that use shadow DOM + contenteditable, a legitimate and growing web pattern.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: WebKit locator.fill() doesn't work for contenteditable inside shadow DOM
source_issues.evidence: Regression from 1.58.2 to 1.59.0: WebKit returns {textContent: '', innerText: ''} for contenteditable fill in shadow DOM, while Chromium correctly shows 'Hello'. The operation reports no error but silently fails. Also affects Vitest browser mode users.

signals.topic: Python AgentGroupChat fails with 'Unknown response format' when Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled, blocking all multi-agent executions
signals.summary: When Azure Monitor (configure_azure_monitor) is enabled with AzureAIAgent inside AgentGroupChat, all agent executions fail with ValueError: Unknown response format <class 'dict'>. The Azure AI telemetry instrumentor does not support dict type response_format, breaking the multi-agent flow entirely.
aliases: OpenTelemetry instrumentor incompatible with dict response_format
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：Azure Monitor遥测拦截导致AgentGroupChat所有执行失败，多智能体工作流完全不可用。用户明确报告App Insights日志中反复重试后最终失败，且无任何workaround。

source_issues.title: Bug: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with 'Unknown response format <class 'dict'>' when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: All agent executions fail with ValueError when Azure Monitor is enabled. Multi-agent flow is completely blocked. App Insights logs show repeated retry attempts followed by final failure.

signals.topic: .NET Gemini streaming connector emits duplicate OpenTelemetry token usage metrics per chunk, causing 10-30x inflated cost tracking
signals.summary: The .NET Gemini connector calls LogUsage() for every streaming chunk instead of once at the end, causing OpenTelemetry token counters to accumulate duplicate counts. Production systems show $0.40 logged vs $0.02 actual API cost.
aliases: Gemini token metrics inflated during streaming
Duplicate token usage telemetry in Gemini connector
signals.review_reason: 明确成本损失：生产环境显示实际$0.02的API费用被计为$0.40，计费系统被重复计量20倍。根因明确（每个streaming chunk重复调用LogUsage），且与Python/OpenAI同题修复(#12977)可对比确认。

source_issues.title: Bug: .NET: Gemini connector emits duplicate token usage metrics during streaming
source_issues.evidence: Production systems show $0.40 logged vs $0.02 actual API cost (20x inflation). Metrics emitted per streaming chunk instead of once per API call. Root cause identified in ProcessChatResponseStreamAsync calling LogUsage() for each chunk.

signals.topic: .NET Chat Completion Agent calls functions outside the explicitly provided FunctionChoiceBehavior list (function spillover)
signals.summary: The Chat Completion Agent calls functions that are NOT in the explicitly provided FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto([...]) list, such as save_stop_condition when only load_current_number, save_current_number, and increment_number were allowed. This violates documented behavior and creates security/reliability issues.
aliases: Agent calls out-of-scope functions despite explicit whitelist
signals.review_reason: 关键安全/可靠性问题：Agent调用了不在白名单内的函数(save_stop_condition)，违反明确文档行为。用户提供可复现的代码示例和日志证据，且即使移除FunctionChoiceBehavior参数也无法修复，表明执行设置被完全忽略。

source_issues.title: Bug: Functions spillover in Chat Completion Agent
source_issues.evidence: save_stop_condition was called even though it was NOT in FunctionChoiceBehavior.Auto([loadCurrentNumberFunction, saveCurrentNumberFunction, incrementingFunction]). User documented that removing FunctionChoiceBehavior line does not fix it, suggesting execution settings are ignored entirely.

signals.topic: Python: azure-ai-agents 1.1.0 dependency incompatibility breaks McpTool import in semantic-kernel[Azure]
signals.summary: After upgrading semantic-kernel[Azure] to 1.35.1, McpTool cannot be imported because the azure-ai-agents dependency version pinned in SK (>=1.1.0b4) resolves to 1.1.0 stable which removed McpTool class.
aliases: McpTool import fails due to azure-ai-agents version conflict
semantic-kernel dependency on azure-ai-agents pins incompatible version
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：McpTool是MCP(Machine Control Protocol)集成的核心组件，依赖版本不兼容导致整个MCP功能无法使用。用户提供明确的import错误和版本冲突证据。

source_issues.title: Bug: Python - Semantic Kernel 1.35.1 is missing McpTools due to azure-ai-agents 1.1.0
source_issues.evidence: McpTool import fails after upgrading to semantic-kernel[Azure]>=1.35.1. azure-ai-agents 1.1.0 stable released Aug 5 removed McpTool class that was present in beta versions. User blocked from using MCP functionality.

signals.topic: .NET: MCP tool names with dashes throw ArgumentException during AsKernelFunction conversion, blocking MCP server integration
signals.summary: When converting MCP client tools to Kernel Functions using AsKernelFunction(), tool names containing dashes (e.g., 'create-pages') cause System.ArgumentException because plugin names can only contain ASCII letters, digits, and underscores.
aliases: MCP tool name dash conversion fails
AsKernelFunction rejects MCP tool names with hyphens
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：MCP工具名称中包含dash是标准约定(如'create-pages')，但SK强制要求plugin名称只能包含字母数字和下划线，导致所有带dash名称的MCP服务器无法集成。用户提供可复现代码和完整错误堆栈。

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Converting MCP Tools to Kernel Function Throws System.ArgumentException
source_issues.evidence: System.ArgumentException: A plugin name can contain only ASCII letters, digits, and underscores: 'create-pages' is not a valid name. MCP server uses dash-separated tool names (standard naming convention), blocking all MCP server integrations.

signals.topic: MCP tool integration silently fails — Figma reads timeout, Playwright MCP ignored, tools not exposed to model
signals.summary: Codex reports MCP servers as enabled but tool calls either timeout (Figma), are ignored (Playwright), or tools are not exposed to the model despite successful registration. Creates false-green health state where MCP appears working but tools are unavailable.
aliases: MCP tools not exposed to model
signals.review_reason: 4 distinct MCP integration failures across 4 separate issues all share the same root pattern: Codex confirms MCP server is running but tool execution either times out, is routed to wrong path, or tools are not visible to the model. This creates a false-green state where users believe MCP is configured correctly, wasting investigation time and blocking workflows (Figma UI implementation, Playwright browser automation). The false-green nature makes this especially insidious — users don't know their tools aren't actually available until explicit test failures occur.

source_issues.title: Figma plugin reads time out after 120s
source_issues.evidence: Figma MCP authenticated (whoami works) but all file reads hang until 120s tool timeout or upstream transport reset. Blocks Figma-driven UI implementation even though plugin is visibly connected.

source_issues.title: Codex desktop can show MCP enabled while thread tool surface omits llm-tldr/serena
source_issues.evidence: codex mcp list shows MCP servers as 'enabled', backing processes alive, but thread_dynamic_tools table empty — model cannot call tools. Silent degradation with no error surfaced.

source_issues.title: Codex desktop ignores configured Playwright MCP server and falls back to Chrome-launching Playwright path
source_issues.evidence: Playwright MCP server configured and running (npx @playwright/mcp@latest processes alive), codex mcp list shows enabled, but tool calls fail with 'chrome executable not found' — desktop app routes through wrong path instead of configured MCP.

source_issues.title: Codex-side MCP discovery/display bug or limitation
source_issues.evidence: Local stdio MCP server starts successfully and logs 15 registered tools, but Codex TUI shows 'Tools: (none)'. Ruled out server-side causes; suggests Codex is either not issuing tools/list or not surfacing results in UI.

signals.topic: Model output quality degradation — off-topic/lengthy responses and reduced code generation accuracy
signals.summary: Users report that Codex model produces off-topic, ungrammatical, overly lengthy responses after certain prompts (e.g., security-related queries), and exhibits performance degradation including missing easy bugs and lazy behavior.
signals.review_reason: Three separate reports of model output quality degradation: (1) off-topic and grammatically incorrect lengthy responses after a specific trigger, (2) performance degradation with missed easy bugs, (3) suboptimal tool selection (devtools instead of read). These undermine the core value proposition of a code generation tool. The first issue is particularly concerning as it appears triggered by a security-related prompt, suggesting potential prompt injection sensitivity.

source_issues.title: Completely unrelated and lengthy response
source_issues.evidence: After asking about a compromised Axios NPM package, Codex output became completely unrelated, extremely lengthy, meaningless, and full of bad grammar. User has thread recording. Clear output quality degradation with specific trigger context.

source_issues.title: GPT 5.4 Performance degradation
source_issues.evidence: GPT-5.4-codex model performance degrading — missing easy bugs and being lazy. User provides thread ID with evidence. Impacts core coding assistant value proposition.

source_issues.title: codex is using chrome devtools to read files instead of the default read
source_issues.evidence: Model choosing chrome devtools to read files instead of default read tool. User expects model to prefer 'read' tool. Affects tool selection quality and potentially accuracy of code analysis.

signals.topic: Codex Web screenshot generation regression — visual preview feature completely unavailable
signals.summary: Codex Web screenshot tool stopped working entirely a couple of weeks ago for all React and Node projects, displaying a 'browser screenshot tool not available' error instead of generating screenshots. This was a differentiating feature that companies relied on for non-technical stakeholder validation.
aliases: browser screenshot tool not available error on web
visual preview broken in Codex Web
signals.review_reason: Explicit regression: the screenshot feature worked in early March and stopped without user configuration changes. The user explicitly states this was a differentiating feature driving their company's choice of Codex over alternatives — it enabled non-technical reviewers to validate AI-generated changes without needing to run a local environment. This is a key workflow feature that went from working to broken with no user recourse.

source_issues.title: Codex Web Screenshots Are Not anymore available
source_issues.evidence: Regression — worked fine until early March. Now every React/Angular project returns 'browser screenshot tool not available in this environment' on Codex Web. Company explicitly states screenshots were a reason they chose Codex over alternatives, as they enable non-technical stakeholders to validate changes without running environments.

signals.topic: Azure OpenAI / custom OpenAI-compatible base URL completely ignored — all requests routed to api.openai.com
signals.summary: Codex CLI ignores both openai_base_url config setting and OPENAI_BASE_URL environment variable. All requests always go to api.openai.com regardless of configuration, making Azure OpenAI integration impossible and blocking use of $100K sponsorship credits.
signals.review_reason: Clear blocking bug: the openai_base_url configuration is completely non-functional across all three configuration methods (config file, env var, CLI flag). This directly prevents Azure OpenAI users — a major enterprise use case — from using the tool with their API endpoints. The user has $100K in Azure credits they cannot use with Codex, which represents a concrete cost/opportunity loss.

source_issues.title: openai_base_url config and OPENAI_BASE_URL env var are ignored — always calls api.openai.com
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly blocked from using $100K Azure OpenAI sponsorship credits. Tried config.toml setting, OPENAI_BASE_URL env var, and CLI flag — all ignored. Local proxy on configured port receives zero requests. Same Azure API works fine via curl. Blocks enterprise deployment.

signals.topic: Interactive CLI hangs or becomes extremely slow on multi-command / branching / complex agentic turns
signals.summary: Interactive Codex CLI TUI gets stuck on 'Working...' for multi-command, branching, retry-heavy, background-terminal-heavy, or longer-lived turns, even when codex exec handles the same tasks reliably. Reproduces across Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows — appears specific to interactive TUI orchestration path.
aliases: interactive CLI hangs on complex tasks
TUI stuck on Working during agentic turns
interactive mode degradation on multi-command tasks
signals.review_reason: This is a core workflow blocker affecting the primary use case of the CLI. The interactive mode — which is the intended agent experience — fails on multi-command tasks while the batch 'codex exec' path works for the same prompts. This means the most natural way to use Codex as an interactive coding assistant is unreliable, forcing users to fall back to a less ergonomic workaround. Cross-platform reproduction (3 OSes) and persistence across two versions establish strong evidence.

source_issues.title: Interactive CLI hangs on multi-command / branching turns
source_issues.evidence: Reproduces across 3 OSes (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows). Same complex prompts work reliably via 'codex exec' but hang indefinitely in interactive mode. User must fall back to codex exec workaround which lacks intended interactive agent workflow. Tested on both stable (0.118.0) and prerelease (0.119.0-alpha.4) — issue persists.

signals.topic: GPT-5.1/GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests with no error/timeout/retry
signals.summary: The /v1/responses endpoint silently drops 10-28% of concurrent requests under moderate load, leaving TCP connections hanging indefinitely with no HTTP error, no timeout, and no SDK retry. Both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK Runner.run() are equally affected, confirming server-side origin but impacting all SDK users.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocked: 10-28% of concurrent requests hang silently with no error, no timeout, and no retry from SDK. User provides reproducible test scripts across 4 runs with quantified evidence. Both raw client and Agents SDK are equally affected, confirming the /v1/responses endpoint is the root cause but impacting ALL SDK users relying on that endpoint.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible across 4 test runs with 50 calls each. Raw AsyncOpenAI.responses.create() hangs at 20%; Agents SDK Runner.run() hangs at 24%. Hung requests receive no HTTP response, no error, no retry — TCP connection hangs indefinitely until caller timeout. Confirmed via cf-ray headers to be server-side (OpenAI API endpoint). Affects gpt-5.1 and gpt-5.4-2026-03-05.

signals.topic: Prompt caching drops to 0% when base64 file inputs are introduced in mixed text/file request flows
signals.summary: When switching from text-only to file-input requests, prompt cache hit rate collapses from ~97% to 0% even though the prompt prefix, system instructions, and tool definitions remain unchanged. This causes significant cost increase for production agents using mixed inputs.
aliases: prompt cache invalidation on file input
base64 file input breaks prompt cache prefix matching
signals.review_reason: Clear cost impact: cache hit drops from 96.7% to 0% when file inputs are introduced in a mixed-flow conversation. Even though the shared prefix (13k tokens), system instructions, and tool definitions remain unchanged, the API treats the request as a new cache key. This causes direct cost increase for production agents that mix text and file inputs — a significant financial impact. Reproducible across multiple rounds with consistent behavior.

source_issues.title: Prompt caching drops to 0% when introducing base64 file inputs
source_issues.evidence: Consistent reproducible behavior: text-only rounds yield 96.7% cache hit; adding a base64 PDF file input drops cache to 0%; repeating same file restores ~90.3% cache. The prompt prefix, tool definitions, and system instructions are identical across rounds. Only the user message varies. Cache key parameter has zero impact. Observed via both Agents SDK and Responses API directly.

signals.topic: Preambles/commentary messages not generated when output_type (structured output) is set
signals.summary: When output_type is set (mapped to text.format: json_schema), the model skips the preamble/commentary phase entirely and jumps straight to tool calls, creating a noticeable UX dead zone where users see nothing while tools execute.
signals.review_reason: UX degradation when combining structured output with tool use: the preamble/commentary message that provides user acknowledgment before tool execution is entirely suppressed when output_type is set (json_schema format). Users experience a silent dead zone — no streaming feedback while tools execute — which is a significant perceived latency issue. The user explicitly describes this as a known UX dead zone and asks for a workaround.

source_issues.title: Preambles with structured output
source_issues.evidence: With output_type set, ResponseOutputMessage phase=commentary disappears entirely; model jumps straight to ResponseFunctionToolCall. Without output_type, phase=commentary message appears correctly before tool call. User explicitly describes the dead zone: 'Without preambles, there's a noticeable dead zone where nothing is streamed to the user while the tool runs.' The API documentation confirms preambles should appear before tool calls.

signals.topic: Gemini 3 Pro Preview requires thought_signature on follow-up calls but Agents SDK does not inject it, causing BadRequestError on multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: The Agents SDK fails to propagate thought_signature across turns when using Gemini 3 Pro Preview with OpenAIChatCompletionsModel, breaking multi-turn tool-use conversations with a BadRequestError.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocked for multi-turn Gemini 3 Pro conversations: the SDK fails to propagate thought_signature across turns, causing a BadRequestError on the second interaction. Plain OpenAI client works correctly, confirming the bug is in SDK conversation history management. Multi-turn tool-use workflows with Gemini 3 Pro are completely broken.

source_issues.title: Missing thought_signature when using Gemini 3 pro preview
source_issues.evidence: openai.BadRequestError: function call in the 2nd content block is missing a thought_signature. The thought_signature returned by the first response is not injected by the SDK into subsequent conversation history. Plain OpenAI client correctly propagates it; Agents SDK + Runner.run() does not. Multi-turn tool-call conversations are completely blocked.

signals.topic: No built-in support for rewind/delete/retry of the last user message in persistent sessions, forcing fragile manual workarounds
signals.summary: The Agents SDK lacks a public API to rewind, delete, or edit the last user turn in a persistent session. Users building chat UIs must manually walk backward through flat history lists, which is fragile with multi-agent handoffs and multi-turn tool calls.
aliases: session history rewind not exposed publicly
signals.review_reason: Common chat UX pattern (delete/retry/edit) has no public SDK API for persistent sessions, forcing developers to implement fragile manual history manipulation. While not a crash/blocker, the lack of a supported pattern means every production app building a chat interface must reinvent fragile workarounds. Compared to Google ADK which exposes rewind_async() as a first-class API, the SDK leaves users without guidance.

source_issues.title: Best strategy for delete / retry / edit last user message (rewind equivalent)
source_issues.evidence: No public API for rewind/undo of the last turn in a session. Internal rewind_input() exists for conversation_locked errors but is not public. Google ADK has runner.rewind_async() as a first-class operation. Users building production chat UIs (PostgreSQL-backed sessions) have no supported way to implement delete/retry/edit, forcing fragile manual history manipulation that breaks with multi-agent handoffs.

signals.topic: Custom API base URL requests blocked with OpenAIException 'Your request was blocked'
signals.summary: When using a custom API base URL (e.g., a local LLM studio), all requests fail with OpenAIException 'Your request was blocked'. The same requests work correctly with the requests library directly or with litellm, confirming the issue is within the OpenAI Python SDK's request handling for custom bases.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports of custom API base usage being blocked or returning 502 errors, preventing users from using local LLM backends (LMStudio) and custom endpoints. Affects a legitimate use case (local model hosting). Second report includes full stack trace confirming SDK as the source of the blocking behavior.

source_issues.title: OpenAIException – 'Your request was blocked' with custom API base
source_issues.evidence: Custom API base URL causes all requests to fail with 'Your request was blocked'. Verified same request works with direct requests library and litellm. SDK adds something (headers/traffic) that triggers blocking at the custom endpoint.

source_issues.title: windows call lmstudio (127.0.0.1:1234/v1), get 502
source_issues.evidence: Windows user connecting to local LMStudio (127.0.0.1:1234/v1) receives HTTP 502 InternalServerError via SDK, causing the request to fail entirely. Same configuration should work for local LLM endpoints.

signals.topic: /v1/responses endpoint silently hangs 10–28% of concurrent requests causing indefinite TCP connection hangs
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load (5 simultaneous calls), the /v1/responses endpoint silently drops 10–28% of requests. Affected requests receive no HTTP error, no timeout, and no SDK retry — TCP connections hang indefinitely until the caller kills them. Reproducible across GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.4-2026-03-05, confirmed to affect both raw AsyncOpenAI client and Agents SDK Runner.run() equally, ruling out SDK involvement.
signals.review_reason: High-frequency main-flow blocking issue (10–28% request loss rate under concurrency). No error returned, no SDK retry, indefinite TCP hang — completely silently absorbs failures. Confirmed with multiple test runs, affects both raw SDK and Agents SDK equally, proven server-side by cf-ray headers. High user impact: production workflows silently lose requests.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible 10–28% hang rate across multiple test runs with raw AsyncOpenAI client and Agents SDK. 4 test runs (50 calls each) showing 8%–28% hung rate. HTTP connection accepted (TCP handshake completes) but no response ever returned. No retry triggered in SDK because no error is received. Requests hang until caller timeout kills them.

signals.topic: Responses WebSocket (/v1/responses) closes with code 1000 and no events when temperature is a decimal value
signals.summary: Calling responses.create over WebSocket (wss://api.openai.com/v1/responses) with a decimal temperature (e.g., 1.2) immediately closes the connection with code 1000 and zero events. Integer temperatures (e.g., 1) work fine. The API docs state temperature is numeric, implying decimals should be accepted.
signals.review_reason: Key feature (/v1/responses WebSocket) breaks silently for any user passing decimal temperature values — a common configuration. No error event returned, just a clean 1000 close, making debugging difficult. Clear regression against API documentation stating temperature is numeric.

source_issues.title: Responses WebSocket (/v1/responses) closes with code 1000 and no events when temperature is a decimal (e.g., 1.2)
source_issues.evidence: WebSocket connection closes immediately with code 1000 (normal closure) and zero events when temperature is a decimal value (1.2). Integer value 1 works correctly. The behavior is silent and non-obvious — users would not know why their request fails. Reproduction script provided showing the exact payload.

signals.topic: 安全扫描误报率高，众多合法技能被错误标记为 suspicious，阻塞发布并增加人工审核负担
signals.summary: 至少 12 个 issue 反映了同一核心问题：ClawHub 安全扫描将众多合法技能（安全工具、企业 MCP 工具、视频编辑、支付、文档管理等）错误标记为 suspicious/flagged，导致技能无法正常展示/安装，需要用户提交人工审核申诉，且部分申诉缺乏具体原因说明。
signals.review_reason: 高频误报问题（12 个独立 issue）造成明确用户体验损害：合法技能被标记后无法正常展示/安装，用户需提交人工申诉等待审核，严重阻塞发布流程；且部分申诉缺乏具体触发原因说明（仅笼统称 suspicious patterns），用户体验摩擦显著。

source_issues.title: [False Positive] SafeClaw Security Auditor flagged as malicious

signals.topic: Device authentication and pairing failures cause node connection blocking
signals.summary: Three distinct but related bugs all cause device-to-gateway authentication or pairing to fail, resulting in nodes being stuck in Connecting or Disconnected states with no automatic recovery. Issues include: (1) signature mode fallback never re-sends connect after rejection, leaving WebSocket open but unauthenticated; (2) hello-ok never includes auth.deviceToken, preventing durable reconnection; (3) node mode shows Disconnected with no device pairing request reaching the server.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct auth/pairing bugs with clear user-impact evidence: (131) client permanently stuck in Connecting if initial signature rejected; (81) device token never persisted, forcing repeated manual gateway approvals; (114) node mode silently fails with no pairing request reaching the server. All three block the core device-connection workflow with no user-friendly recovery. Count=3 from the same repo but represent distinct root causes sharing the same high-level theme. Downgraded to P1 since the evidence for #114 is labeled 'needs investigation' and lacks root-cause detail.

source_issues.title: Bug: Signature mode fallback never retries connect message
source_issues.evidence: Client stuck in Connecting state after gateway rejects device signature — WebSocket open but unauthenticated with no automatic retry. Fix requires either re-sending SendConnectMessageAsync or forcing a reconnect cycle.

source_issues.title: Missing deviceToken
source_issues.evidence: hello-ok response missing auth.deviceToken after device approval. Client cannot persist device token for future reconnects — every reconnect requires re-approval on the gateway side, breaking the reconnection story entirely.

source_issues.title: Node mode not work
source_issues.evidence: With node mode enabled and gateway connected, status shows Connected but Node Mode shows Disconnected. Server-side logs show zero device pairing requests, indicating the node registration message is never emitted or received.

signals.topic: Notification sound setting ignored — user sound preference never applied to toast notifications
signals.summary: The NotificationSound setting in tray settings is saved correctly but is never read when building toast notifications. All toast calls in App.xaml.cs use ToastContentBuilder().Show() directly without applying the sound preference, causing toasts to always play default sounds regardless of user preference. Same root cause affects two separate PRs (#71 and #92).
aliases: sound preference saved but never applied
signals.review_reason: Two separate PRs created for the same root cause (automation agent generated #71 as a bug report, then #92 as the fix). User's sound preference is silently ignored — every toast notification plays default sound regardless of settings. While not blocking, this is a persistent UX regression affecting every notification, and two independent PRs confirm the pattern.

source_issues.title: [Repo Assist] bug: NotificationSound setting has no effect — sound is never applied to toast notifications
source_issues.evidence: Sound combo box in Settings saves correctly but the value is never read when building toast notifications. All toast Show() calls bypass any sound preference.

source_issues.title: [Repo Assist] fix: apply NotificationSound setting to all toast notifications
source_issues.evidence: Introduces ShowToast(ToastContentBuilder) helper that reads _settings.Settings.NotificationSound and applies Silent=true via AddAudio when disabled. Fixes the root cause of #71.

signals.topic: SSH tunnel unexpected exit leaves remote connectivity permanently broken without auto-recovery
signals.summary: SshTunnelService only logs a warning when the SSH tunnel process exits unexpectedly. It does not clean up internal state, raise any event, or attempt a restart. The gateway client spins in a reconnect loop against a dead localhost port indefinitely, breaking the entire remote connectivity feature until the user manually intervenes.
aliases: SSH tunnel crash causes infinite reconnect loop
tunnel exit leaves dead port with no recovery
signals.review_reason: Main flow feature (remote connectivity) permanently broken after tunnel crash. Infinite reconnect loop against dead port means no auto-recovery is possible — user must manually intervene. Clear process-exit handler gap with confirmed missing recovery logic. Count=1 from single repo, but the impact (permanent feature breakage with no recovery) warrants P1 over P2.

source_issues.title: Bug: SSH tunnel not restarted on unexpected exit
source_issues.evidence: SshTunnelService.process.Exited handler only logs a warning. No cleanup of _process/_lastSpec, no TunnelExited event, no restart attempt. Gateway client reconnects to ws://127.0.0.1:<deadPort> indefinitely. Entire remote connectivity broken until user manually changes settings or restarts the app.

signals.topic: Missing operator.write OAuth scope blocks message sending for operators
signals.summary: Operators using the messaging API receive 'missing scope: operator.write' errors. Both the demo's quick-send feature and custom clients fail to send messages. The required OAuth scope is not present in the client's token, making the entire messaging functionality unusable for operator users.
signals.review_reason: Core messaging feature is completely non-functional for operator users due to missing OAuth scope. Both custom clients and the built-in demo quick-send fail with the same error. While only one issue, the impact (full feature outage for an entire user role) justifies P1.

source_issues.title: I developed a client to send messages to openclaw, but it consistently fails to send
source_issues.evidence: Gateway request returns 'missing scope: operator.write'. Both custom client and demo quick-send fail identically with this error. Messaging feature is completely non-functional for operators.

signals.topic: Custom notification UserRules feature completely non-functional due to missing parameter at call sites
signals.summary: NotificationCategorizer.Classify() accepts an optional userRules parameter for custom notification rules (step 3 of the categorization pipeline). Both call sites in OpenClawGatewayClient — EmitNotification and EmitChatNotification — call Classify() without passing userRules. This silently makes the entire UserRules feature non-functional: any custom rules saved in Settings are completely ignored.
aliases: custom notification classification rules never applied
signals.review_reason: A feature appears fully functional (no error messages) but silently does nothing. User-defined rules are persisted to Settings but completely ignored at runtime with no indication of failure. This is a silent data-loss quality issue affecting the notification customization workflow. Count=1 and non-blocking, so P2.

source_issues.title: [Repo Assist] fix: pass UserRules to NotificationCategorizer in OpenClawGatewayClient
source_issues.evidence: Both call sites in OpenClawGatewayClient call Classify() without passing user rules. Custom notification rules saved in Settings are silently ignored — the feature appears to work (no errors) but never applies any user-defined rules.

signals.review_reason: Count=3 confirmed regression causing 8-12s delays (vs expected sub-second) on the primary user interaction flow. Cumulative latency increases with each message, making continued conversation progressively slower. All users upgrading past v2026.2.26 are affected.

signals.topic: Uncaught ValueError in exceptions.py: litellm exceptions list out of sync causing crash during message send or startup
signals.summary: When litellm adds new exception classes (e.g., PermissionDeniedError) that aren't registered in aider's LiteLLMExceptions list, an uncaught ValueError is raised at send_message() or model init, crashing the entire application. Two distinct litellm exception names affected (PermissionDeniedError and ConnectionTimeoutError) with identical root cause.
aliases: ValueError: PermissionDeniedError not in aider exceptions
signals.review_reason: count=2 (plus 1 same-root-cause) with distinct litellm exception names (PermissionDeniedError, ConnectionTimeoutError), all causing uncaught exceptions that crash the main flow. Evidence is explicit stack traces showing crashes at core code paths (send_message, model init). No workaround available to users.

source_issues.title: Uncaught ValueError in exceptions.py line 71

signals.review_reason: count=2 on same root cause (Windows cp1252 console + Unicode in Rich output). Both are uncaught exceptions crashing the application at startup, confirmed on Windows 11. No user workaround available without modifying system locale.
