signals.topic: Provider config parameters leak across providers in multi-provider eval causing API 403 errors
signals.summary: When running multiple OpenAI providers in a single eval, max_tokens config from one provider leaks to other providers that don't explicitly set it, causing HTTP 403 failures on newer models that reject max_tokens (require max_completion_tokens instead).
signals.review_reason: This is a config isolation bug that directly blocks the core multi-provider evaluation workflow. Users cannot run mixed model family evals without workaround (separate --filter-providers runs). The 403 error from a parameter leak is a clear failure in a primary workflow path, even though count=1. The workaround of splitting into separate eval commands is non-trivial and defeats the purpose of multi-provider comparison.

source_issues.title: max_tokens config leaks across providers in multi-provider eval
source_issues.evidence: Setting max_tokens on gpt-4.1-mini causes that parameter to also be sent to gpt-5.4-mini API calls. gpt-5.4-mini fails with HTTP 403 because the model family rejects max_tokens and only accepts max_completion_tokens. Multi-provider eval workflow is entirely blocked.

signals.topic: openai:agents built-in provider cannot handle multimodal (image) inputs in evals
signals.summary: The built-in openai:agents provider passes prompts as plain strings, which causes multimodal content (base64-encoded images) to be rendered as raw text instead of vision content blocks, making image-based evals fail silently.
aliases: image input not passed to agent
signals.review_reason: This blocks the multimodal evaluation workflow — a key capability for production LLM apps that process images. The built-in provider silently converts image payloads to raw text, causing eval failures without clear error messages. Users must write a custom TypeScript provider to work around this, which also bypasses built-in rate limiting and retries. Even though count=1, the failure mode (silent incorrect evaluation results) and workaround complexity make this a high-priority pain point.

source_issues.title: openai:agents built-in provider cannot pass multimodal (image) input to the agent
source_issues.evidence: Provider passes rendered prompt as a plain string to run(). String inputs are converted to plain text user messages. Images embedded via {{image_b64}} are received as raw base64 text instead of {type: 'input_image'} vision blocks. Model cannot see the image and evals fail.

signals.topic: LLM judge models reload repeatedly between rows in multi-judge eval, causing severe performance overhead
signals.summary: When using multiple model-graded assertions (llm-ramric) with local models like ollama, each evaluation row triggers unload/reload cycles for judge models, making multi-judge evals extremely slow due to hardware constraints allowing only one model loaded at a time.
signals.review_reason: This causes significant cost (repeated model loading) and time overhead for users running model-graded assertions. While not a hard failure, it makes multi-judge evaluation workflows impractical on resource-constrained hardware, directly impacting the core evaluation workflow. Users have no in-product workaround — the only option is running fewer judges or more powerful hardware.

source_issues.title: Batch judge evaluation to avoid model reload overhead
source_issues.evidence: User has hardware constraints allowing only one judge model loaded at a time. With multiple judges configured, ollama unloads and reloads models for every single evaluation row. No batching configuration exists to group all evaluations by Judge 1 before switching to Judge 2.

signals.topic: BasicMCPClient.get_prompt() raises NotImplementedError on valid MCP EmbeddedResource/AudioContent types, breaking primary MCP prompt flow
signals.summary: BasicMCPClient.get_prompt() only handles TextContent and ImageContent. For EmbeddedResource, AudioContent, and ResourceLink types (spec-valid MCP ContentBlock variants), it raises NotImplementedError or ValueError, causing the entire MCP prompt pipeline to fail with a full exception stack trace.
aliases: MCP client fails on AudioContent ResourceLink types
signals.review_reason: Primary MCP prompt pipeline is completely blocked for valid MCP spec-compliant content types. Full stack trace provided. Not a hypothetical — confirmed reproducible with the official MCP everything server. Blocks any agent using MCP tools that return EmbeddedResource, AudioContent, or ResourceLink in prompts.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: `BasicMCPClient.get_prompt()` fails on valid MCP `ContentBlock` types
source_issues.evidence: Full exception traceback shows NotImplementedError: Embedded resources are not supported yet. Triggered by calling get_prompt() on official MCP reference server with EmbeddedResource content type. Affects llama-index-tools-mcp 0.4.8 and llama-index-core 0.14.19.

signals.topic: Refine synthesizer uncaught ValueError/TypeError crashes query engine when function-calling LLM structured outputs fail
signals.summary: Refine._give_response_single only catches ValidationError for output_cls structured outputs. When function-calling LLMs raise ValueError (no tool calls) or TypeError (non-BaseModel output), these are uncaught and the entire query fails instead of taking the warning fallback path.
aliases: Refine response synthesizer crash on ValueError from structured predict
output_cls query fails with uncaught exception instead of graceful degradation
signals.review_reason: Core response synthesizer crashes instead of gracefully degrading for a common failure mode (function-calling LLM not returning tool calls). This is a primary query engine path that should have graceful fallback, not an unhandled exception. Root cause is clear (#21036 changes) and repro is provided.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Refine does not catch `ValueError`/`TypeError` from tool-calling structured outputs
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace shows ValueError propagating through query_engine → response_synthesizer → refine.py _give_response_single. Repro provided with mocked FunctionCallingProgram raising ValueError. Introduced after v0.14.18 in changes from PR #21036.

signals.topic: Ollama stream_chat/astream_chat silently drops thinking-only chunks, losing all extended thinking output during streaming
signals.summary: When streaming from Ollama models with extended thinking (DeepSeek-R1, QwQ), chunks where content=None but thinking is present are silently skipped by a guard in stream_chat/astream_chat. Non-streaming chat() correctly returns thinking content; streaming loses it entirely.
aliases: stream_chat skips thinking-only chunks for DeepSeek-R1 QwQ
signals.review_reason: Significant user experience degradation for Ollama extended-thinking models during streaming — all reasoning output is silently lost while non-streaming works correctly. Root cause is precisely identified. However, count=1 and only affects one integration (Ollama), not a primary flow blocker for all users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: stream_chat / astream_chat in llama-index-llms-ollama drops thinking-only chunks
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: guard 'if r["message"]["content"] is None: continue' in stream_chat (~line 474) and astream_chat (~line 558) skips thinking-only chunks before ThinkingBlock accumulation logic runs. Repro script shows streaming receives 0 thinking chunks vs non-streaming which correctly returns thinking. Affects llama-index-llms-ollama 0.10.1 with DeepSeek-R1.

signals.topic: LlamaCloud v2 extract API endpoint returns 422 with documented field names and 500 with actual field names, making extraction pipeline unusable
signals.summary: The POST /api/v2/extract endpoint has a field name mismatch: API docs say use type/value, but those return 422. The field names suggested by the 422 error (document_input_type/document_input_value) then cause a 500 server error. The v1 flow works fine with the same documents and schemas.
aliases: API v2 extract endpoint field name mismatch causes extraction failure
signals.review_reason: API endpoint is completely broken — users cannot use the documented API (422) nor the suggested field names (500). This blocks the entire LlamaCloud v2 document extraction pipeline. The issue being closed does not mean the user impact was resolved; it indicates the issue was addressed or abandoned without confirmed fix evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: LlamaCloud `POST /api/v2/extract` — 422 with documented field names, 500 with actual field names
source_issues.evidence: Two distinct HTTP errors confirmed via curl repro: documented fields type/value → 422 'Field required' for document_input_value; actual fields document_input_type/document_input_value → 500 with correlation IDs. Issue closed but the bug indicates a broken API contract.

signals.topic: MCP tools are not automatically used — advertised 'just use Claude Code normally' workflow is non-functional
signals.summary: After `ruflo init --full`, MCP tools are registered but Claude never calls them because tools are 'deferred' and require ToolSearch. Hook output is passive text with no mechanism to force tool invocation. This was independently reported by multiple users and is explicitly acknowledged as contradicting the README promise. Issue #1511 confirms the same root cause: generated CLAUDE.md has no ToolSearch bootstrap or hook signal binding, so Claude ignores/simulates all ruflo features.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow failure: the product's flagship promise ('just use Claude Code normally') is completely non-functional. Three independent users reported this. Claude ignores all ruflo MCP tools because they are 'deferred' and CLAUDE.md provides no bootstrap. This blocks the core value proposition of the entire product.

source_issues.title: MCP tools are not automatically used — 'just use Claude Code normally' doesn't work
source_issues.evidence: After a full install, hooks fire and MCP tools are registered, but Claude never actually calls any of them. User had to manually create ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md with explicit ToolSearch instructions. Confirmed by #1511: generated CLAUDE.md has no ToolSearch guidance and no hook signal binding.

source_issues.title: Bug: claudemd-generator.ts references 'Task tool' (renamed to 'Agent'), missing ToolSearch/hook signal guidance
source_issues.evidence: Independently reported by users in #1476, #1497, and #1491. Generated CLAUDE.md has no ToolSearch bootstrap, no hook signal binding, and phantom signal references. Claude ignores or simulates all ruflo features.

source_issues.title: Make better use of the framework
source_issues.evidence: User set up a full ruflo flow with GitLab polling, Claude dispatch, and swarm tasks, but never sees results from background tasks. Directly cited in #1511 as an affected user.

signals.topic: AgentDB exposes 4 non-functional controllers — tools silently fail with 'not available' errors, blocking core AgentDB features
signals.summary: agentdb_controllers reports 4 active controllers, but ContextSynthesizer, ReasoningBank, BatchOperations, and CausalMemoryGraph bridge are all non-functional. The four dependent MCP tools (context-synthesize, pattern-search, batch, causal-edge) return errors and are exposed in the tool list as if they work. This blocks context synthesis from stored memories, pattern search with confidence scoring, bulk memory operations, and knowledge graph edges.
signals.review_reason: AgentDB's core differentiating features are non-functional. Users see these tools in the MCP tool list and try to use them, only to get silent 'not available' errors. The root cause is clear and fixable (missing embedder param). Blocks context synthesis, pattern-based retrieval, and causal graph features — all key AgentDB capabilities.

source_issues.title: AgentDB: 4 controllers unimplemented (ContextSynthesizer, ReasoningBank, BatchOperations, CausalMemoryGraph bridge)
source_issues.evidence: agentdb_context-synthesize returns 'ContextSynthesizer not available', agentdb_pattern-search returns 'controller: unavailable', agentdb_batch returns 'BatchOperations not available', agentdb_causal-edge returns 'bridge not available'. Root cause: controllers never registered in initializer, missing embedder param causes constructor throws, or bridge doesn't route correctly.

source_issues.title: ReasoningBank controller disabled — missing embedder param in ControllerRegistry
source_issues.evidence: Root cause confirmed: new RB(this.agentdb.database) called with only 1 argument but requires 2 (db, embedder). Constructor throws, catch returns null, registry marks it as enabled:false. Fix documented as 2-line diff. This is the specific cause of pattern-search failure in #1492.

signals.topic: Plugin installation blocked by missing npm package (@claude-flow/ruvector-upstream E404) and semver pre-release mismatch
signals.summary: Two separate issues combine to completely block plugin installation. First, @claude-flow/ruvector-upstream is not published to npm (E404), blocking all plugins that transitively depend on it. Second, plugin peer dependencies declare '>=3.0.0' but only '3.0.0-alpha.x' versions exist; npm semver treats alpha < 3.0.0, so the range fails. Together these make it impossible to install any plugins.
signals.review_reason: Plugin ecosystem is completely blocked. Two independent bugs combine to prevent any plugin installation: a missing npm package and a semver range that excludes all published versions. This is a packaging/release management failure that prevents users from extending the tool.

source_issues.title: @claude-flow/ruvector-upstream not published to npm (E404)
source_issues.evidence: Exact npm error reproduced: 'npm error 404 Not Found - GET https://registry.npmjs.org/@claude-flow%2fruvector-upstream'. Blocks installation of @claude-flow/embeddings, @claude-flow/plugin-code-intelligence, @claude-flow/security.

source_issues.title: Plugin peer deps reject alpha versions (semver pre-release mismatch)
source_issues.evidence: Exact npm error: 'notarget No matching version found for @claude-flow/embeddings@>=3.0.0'. Root cause: plugin-agentic-qe@3.0.0-alpha.4 declares peer dep '>=3.0.0' but only 3.0.0-alpha.1 exists. npm semver: alpha < release, so range fails.

signals.topic: Memory SQLite database path is relative to CWD — data silently lost on MCP server restart with different working directory
signals.summary: The memory database is stored at `{cwd}/.swarm/memory.db`. When the MCP server restarts from a different directory, it creates a new empty database instead of finding the existing one. Stored data appears to vanish. The data is not deleted but orphaned in the old CWD's `.swarm/` directory, making the memory system appear unreliable and causing real knowledge loss between sessions.
aliases: memory database relative path data loss
signals.review_reason: This is a data integrity failure: user knowledge stored in the memory system silently disappears between sessions when working across different projects/directories. The data loss is not immediately obvious (data is orphaned, not deleted), making it especially dangerous. Users lose accumulated context and domain knowledge with no warning.

source_issues.title: Memory SQLite database path is relative to CWD, causing data loss on MCP server restart
source_issues.evidence: Detailed reproduction: store entries from /Users/stuart/project-a, restart server from /Users/stuart/project-b, all entries gone. Database path uses process.cwd() which changes between sessions. Data is orphaned, not deleted. Makes the entire memory system appear unreliable.

signals.topic: ruflo init --full and ruflo init hooks are disconnected — hooks never fire, advertised 'just use normally' automation never works
signals.summary: Two separate init commands exist that must both be run to get a working setup, but neither completes the full job alone. `init --full` creates helper scripts but never updates settings.json. `init hooks` creates settings.json entries but points to scripts that don't exist. This directly causes the MCP tools not auto-used issue (#1497). The README's claim that 'after running init, just use Claude Code normally' is structurally impossible without manual intervention.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary setup failure: the advertised 'one-command setup' does not work. Users following the README get a broken automation system where hooks never fire. This is the architectural root cause of the MCP tools not auto-used pain point (#1497). P0 despite count=1 because the README itself promises this automation and it is structurally impossible to achieve without manual wiring.

source_issues.title: Bug: init --full and init hooks are disconnected — hooks never fire without manual wiring
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: ruflo init --full creates 40+ helper scripts but settings.json has no hooks section. ruflo init hooks creates settings.json entries pointing to missing scripts. User had to manually add global hooks to ~/.claude/settings.json. This is the root cause of #1497.

signals.topic: Upgrade后旧版守护进程未正确退出导致CDP命令静默失败
signals.summary: agent-browser升级后旧daemon进程持续运行，ensure_daemon()仅检测socket连通性而不检查版本，导致get url、cookies get等命令静默返回错误数据，主流程完全阻断。
signals.review_reason: count=2且均为open状态，根因均为daemon管理/版本校验缺失，证据链完整：#1127明确描述升级后旧daemon残留导致CDP静默失败的完整复现路径；#1086明确描述auto connect失败率80%。主流程阻断严重（CDP命令返回错误数据但无报错），用户被迫手动pkill清理。

source_issues.title: Stale daemon after upgrade causes silent CDP failures (no version check)
source_issues.evidence: 升级agent-browser后旧daemon进程持续运行，ensure_daemon()仅检查socket连通性不检查版本，导致--cdp get url返回about:blank而非实际页面、cookies get返回空值，用户无任何报错提示，主流程静默阻断。

source_issues.title: Auto Connect inconsistency
source_issues.evidence: auto connect模式下8/10次失败，仪表盘显示连接到空白daemon而非实际页面，用户无法正常使用自动连接功能。

signals.topic: 会话中断后stale socket/进程状态无法自愈，需手动清理
signals.summary: agent-browser在会话异常中断（进程崩溃、网络断开）后遗留stale socket文件和孤儿Chrome进程，close --all无法清理，后续命令持续失败，直到手动rm socket并kill进程才能恢复。
signals.review_reason: 提供了完整的复现路径（三种中断场景），明确stale socket不自愈且污染后续所有会话，需手动清理才能恢复。属于高严重性会话管理缺陷，主流程阻断有直接证据支撑。

source_issues.title: Codex keeps saying agent browser is "stale" or "stuck" and kills it
source_issues.evidence: 会话异常中断后遗留stale socket文件(default.sock)，Failed to bind socket: Address already in use导致后续所有命令失败；close --all报告无活动会话但进程仍存在；需手动rm -f ~/.agent-browser/default.sock + kill -9才能恢复。主流程完全阻断，属于持续性阻断而非单次失败。

signals.topic: 会话崩溃后遗留孤儿Chrome进程阻止正常Chrome启动
signals.summary: agent-browser会话崩溃或异常退出后，头less Chrome进程树（主进程、GPU helper、Renderer等）未被清理，持续持有profile/socket资源锁，导致用户无法正常启动Chrome，需手动pkill -9。
signals.review_reason: 孤儿Chrome进程直接阻断用户日常使用Chrome的能力（主流程阻断），有明确复现步骤和根因定位（缺少signal handler/process-group kill），属于严重会话生命周期管理缺陷。

source_issues.title: Orphaned headless Chrome processes block normal Chrome from launching
source_issues.evidence: 会话崩溃/异常终止后遗留完整Chrome进程树（包括主进程、GPU helper、Renderer helpers、Crashpad handler），持有profile资源锁，用户正常Chrome无法启动直到手动pkill -9 -f "Google Chrome"，关键用户体验严重受损。

signals.topic: 连接真实浏览器会话时CDP attach无限挂起
signals.summary: 通过WebSocket直接连接已运行的Chromium真实会话时，用户批准远程调试提示后agent-browser无限挂起，而相同会话下raw CDP可正常控制页面。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断证据充分（无限挂起且raw CDP对照实验证明非浏览器问题），根因定位到attach流程缺少resume步骤。但count=1且为单仓问题，降级为P1。

source_issues.title: Direct CDP attach to real browser session hangs after approval; raw CDP works after Runtime.runIfDebugger
source_issues.evidence: 通过ws://127.0.0.1:9222/devtools/browser连接真实运行中的Chromium会话，用户批准调试授权后agent-browser无限挂起；同会话下raw CDP在调用Runtime.runIfWaitingForDebugger后可正常工作，证明浏览器可控但agent-browser的attach流程未完成resume步骤，主流程完全阻断。

signals.topic: auto_launch()忽略AGENT_BROWSER_PROVIDER环境变量，强制回退本地Chrome
signals.summary: 设置cloud provider(agentcore)后，auto_launch()不检查AGENT_BROWSER_PROVIDER直接启动本地Chrome，导致cloud provider使用场景完全不可用。
aliases: cloud provider fallback to local chrome
signals.review_reason: cloud provider场景完全阻断，auto_launch()无视配置直接启动本地Chrome，有完整Docker复现环境和/proc/environ证据。count=1但影响明确，属于关键配置逻辑缺陷。

source_issues.title: fix(native): auto_launch() ignores AGENT_BROWSER_PROVIDER, falls back to local Chrome
source_issues.evidence: 配置AGENT_BROWSER_PROVIDER=agentcore后，auto_launch()仍启动本地Chrome导致Auto-launch failed: Chrome exited early；daemon /proc/Pid/environ确认AGENT_BROWSER_PROVIDER=agentcore已注入但被忽略，cloud provider使用场景完全不可用。

signals.topic: SKILL.md zip upload fails with XML tag validation error
signals.summary: 用户上传 .zip 技能包时，SKILL.md 中的 XML 标签被错误地触发验证拒绝，导致上传流程被阻断。
signals.review_reason: 用户核心上传流程被验证规则阻断。虽然 count=1，但该问题直接对应上传发布主流程，且错误信息暗示验证逻辑存在误报（description 中的 XML 标签被错误拦截），是明确的用户体验阻断点。

source_issues.title: Upload Fails with "SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags" Error
source_issues.evidence: 用户尝试上传 react-view-transitions.zip 时，被提示 'SKILL.md description cannot contain XML tags' 错误，上传流程完全阻断。

signals.topic: Compound Component 模式（点号命名空间导入）在 React Server Components 中不被支持
signals.summary: 在 React Server Components（RSC）场景下，使用 Compound Component 模式（如 Things.A / Things.B）进行点号导入会被拒绝，阻碍了使用该模式的 Next.js 开发者使用 RSC。
signals.review_reason: Compound Component 是 React 生态中广泛使用的设计模式，其在 RSC 中的不可用会直接阻断使用该模式的开发者迁移或使用 RSC。虽然仅单条 issue，但根因为 RSC 框架级限制而非仓库自身问题，影响范围超出单一仓库，具备真实用户影响。

source_issues.title: Compound Pattern and RSCs
source_issues.evidence: issue 描述 dot notation 导入（React 推荐的 Compound Component 模式）在 RSC 中不被允许，引用了 Next.js 官方 issue（#51593, #58776），并指出可能与 turbopack 相关。

signals.topic: AWS Bedrock ARN URL encoding bug — inference profiles unusable via @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock
signals.summary: encodeURIComponent encodes slashes and colons in Bedrock application inference profile ARNs, producing invalid endpoint URLs. The Bedrock REST API rejects encoded ARNs, making inference profiles completely non-functional with the official provider.
aliases: bedrock application inference profile not working
signals.review_reason: Two separate but related issues both involve Bedrock ARN handling producing invalid URLs. #14117 shows the Bedrock provider itself rejects encoded ARNs with 400 errors. #14096 shows AI Gateway silently bypasses Bedrock BYOK due to malformed endpoint. Both result in Bedrock being unusable — count=2 confirms this is a recurring pattern, not an isolated case.

source_issues.title: generateText doesn't work with AWS Bedrock application inference profile ARNs
source_issues.evidence: User provides a full reproduction: passing an inference profile ARN as the model ID results in 400 'The provided model identifier is invalid'. Root cause identified as encodeURIComponent encoding slashes and colons. Workaround required building a custom LanguageModelV3 implementation.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway BYOK Bedrock routing fails with empty region in endpoint URL
source_issues.evidence: AI Gateway with BYOK Bedrock credentials fails at the Bedrock provider attempt because the constructed endpoint URL contains an empty region segment (bedrock-runtime..amazonaws.com). The request silently falls back to Anthropic direct, so BYOK Bedrock is never actually used. User cannot leverage their own AWS pricing/quotas.

signals.topic: toolChoice: 'required' does not enforce tool calls — AI skips tool invocation on required turns
signals.summary: When toolChoice is set to 'required', the AI still sometimes fails to call any tool during a turn, contrary to the expected enforced behavior. This breaks agent loops and any flow that relies on mandatory tool use.
signals.review_reason: User reports that toolChoice:'required' does not enforce tool calls, causing AI to skip mandatory tool invocations on every turn. This is a functional gap that breaks agent loops relying on forced tool use. While count=1 (single report), the severity is high as it directly defeats the purpose of the required tool choice configuration.

source_issues.title: Despite using toolChoice: 'required', ai can sometimes not call any tool during a turn.
source_issues.evidence: User reports that with toolChoice:'required' enabled, the AI still bypasses tool calls on every single turn when using OpenRouter models via AI SDK. Agent loop is broken because tools are not called as required.

signals.topic: OpenAI-compatible providerOptions camelCase mismatch — docs say camelCase, implementation requires raw provider name
signals.summary: Documentation states providerOptions key should be camelCase, but the actual chat/completion implementation looks up the raw provider name. Users following the docs get silent failures where provider options are ignored.
signals.review_reason: Doc/implementation inconsistency causes providerOptions to be silently ignored when user follows documented API. This is a clear user-facing bug: options the user explicitly sets have no effect. The mismatch is verified in source code with reproduction provided.

source_issues.title: openai-compatible docs say providerOptions use camelCase, but chat/completion still require the raw provider name
source_issues.evidence: Documentation promises camelCase key lookup for providerOptions, but the implementation uses exact raw provider name lookup. When user follows the documented contract (providerOptions.providerName), options are silently ignored. Only providerOptions['provider-name'] works.

signals.topic: @ai-sdk/google-vertex auth helper recreates GoogleAuth on every call — production latency impact
signals.summary: The Node-side auth helper for @ai-sdk/google-vertex uses object reference equality for cache invalidation, causing GoogleAuth to be recreated on every request when googleAuthOptions is omitted, or when multiple provider instances are created with equivalent credentials. This drops cached auth client state and adds measurable overhead.
signals.review_reason: User reports measurable production latency impact from GoogleAuth being recreated on every request. The bug has two clear triggers: omitted googleAuthOptions (options || {} creates new object each call) and multiple provider instances with equivalent credentials. While count=1, the evidence includes production telemetry observation and a detailed root-cause analysis confirming the mechanism.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/google-vertex Node auth helper recreates GoogleAuth too often due to reference-based cache invalidation
source_issues.evidence: User reports measurable latency difference in production when requests alternate between separately-created provider instances with equivalent credentials. Root cause is reference equality check (options !== authOptions) being true for undefined options because options || {} creates a new object each time. GoogleAuth caching is dropped on every recreation, adding overhead in environments with nontrivial auth flows like workload identity federation.

signals.topic: AI SDK strips empty reasoning text blocks causing Bedrock multi-turn API errors
signals.summary: The SDK drops empty string text blocks from reasoning content in multi-turn conversations with Bedrock. These empty blocks are required by Bedrock API for block index alignment. Dropping them causes index mismatches that trigger validation errors on subsequent turns.
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn Bedrock conversations fail intermittently because empty text blocks (required for block index alignment) are stripped by the SDK. This causes API validation errors on subsequent turns, breaking the core multi-turn conversation flow. The root cause mechanism is clearly documented with before/after block index comparison showing the corruption.

source_issues.title: AI SDK drops "" reasoning blocks but these MUST be included for validation
source_issues.evidence: User reports intermittent Bedrock API errors: 'The model cannot modify thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in assistant messages. These blocks must remain as they were in the original response.' Root cause: SDK strips empty text blocks from reasoning content, corrupting block indices. Step 2 of conversation sends wrong block indices, causing Bedrock to reject the turn.

signals.topic: Multi-zone rewrites render blank page in 16.2.2 (regression from 16.1.7)
signals.summary: Multi-zone rewrite setup (monorepo with rewrites to sub-apps) results in blank white page in 16.2.2 despite sub-app returning HTTP 200. Static assets also return 200 but page is empty. Works correctly in 16.1.7.
signals.review_reason: count=3 (three distinct GitHub issues) with sample repos and reproducible regression. Multi-zone architecture is a critical enterprise feature for monorepo deployments. Blank page means complete functional failure of the proxied application. Downgrade workaround exists but is not acceptable for production.

source_issues.title: [REGRESSION] Multi-zone rewrites render blank page in 16.2.2 (works in 16.1.7)
source_issues.evidence: Monorepo with main app proxying to sub-app via rewrites. Server returns 200 with valid HTML but browser shows blank white page. Downgrading to 16.1.7 resolves immediately. Affects any enterprise monorepo using multi-zone architecture.

source_issues.title: [REGRESSION] Multi-zone rewrites render blank page in 16.2.2 (works in 16.1.7)
source_issues.evidence: Same regression with detailed reproduction steps including assetPrefix configuration. Server logs confirm 200 responses, no ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS. Page completely blank.

source_issues.title: [REGRESSION] Multi-zone rewrites render blank page in 16.2.2 (works in 16.1.7)
source_issues.evidence: Same issue, minimal body. Third independent report of the same regression.

signals.topic: ISR cache poisoning: GET /index with dynamic [slug] route permanently poisons root page cache causing 404
signals.summary: When a dynamic [slug] route handles /index and calls notFound(), it overwrites the root page's ISR cache entry, making the home page permanently return 404. Confirmed in production Kubernetes incident across all pods.
aliases: ISR cache corruption by dynamic route
signals.review_reason: Production K8s incident with permanent 404 on home page, not transient. Root cause identified in source code. Affects any ISR-enabled Next.js app with root-level [slug] and dynamicParams:true.

source_issues.title: `GET /index` with `[slug]` dynamic route poisons ISR cache for `/`, causing permanent 404
source_issues.evidence: Production incident: external client requested GET /index, poisoning ISR cache on all K8s pods and causing home page to return 404. Root cause is resolvedPathname being used as both URL canonicalization key and ISR cache key (ssgCacheKey).

signals.topic: Standalone output OOM: cached internal streamed fetches cause unbounded arrayBuffers growth leading to server crash
signals.summary: Under sustained high-cardinality traffic with output:standalone and cacheComponents:true, the standalone server shows rapid unbounded memory growth and eventually crashes with FATAL ERROR: JavaScript heap out of memory.
aliases: arrayBuffers memory leak in standalone mode
signals.review_reason: Production-grade OOM crash with reproducible load test. Affects self-hosted standalone deployments (the recommended production target). Memory grows unbounded until process exits, destabilizing the server and causing ECONNRESET/UND_ERR_SOCKET for clients.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16.2.2 standalone + Cache Components: cached internal streamed fetches cause unbounded arrayBuffers growth and OOM
source_issues.evidence: Load test with 64 concurrent connections causes memory to grow from 95MB baseline to 3.43GB over 180s, eventually exiting with OOM. arrayBuffers retained unboundedly. Same app with next start recovers memory after run stops, confirming standalone-specific issue.

signals.topic: Turbopack dev server OOM: heap grows to 17GB+ when idle, crashes after 20-30 minutes
signals.summary: Node.js heap grows continuously from ~500MB to 17GB+ over 20-30 minutes of idle dev server time, then crashes with OOM. Different leak from previously fixed prefetch stream and fast-set-immediate issues.
signals.review_reason: Direct dev experience degradation: the dev server becomes unusable after a short idle period, requiring restart. Blocks development workflow. Heap grows deterministically and eventually crashes, which is a clear memory leak in Turbopack's module evaluation.

source_issues.title: Turbopack dev server OOM: heap grows to 17GB+ when idle (Next.js 16.2.1, Node 24)
source_issues.evidence: Heap grows from ~500MB to 17GB+ over 20-30 minutes idle, then crashes. Stack trace shows Turbopack module evaluation paths (instantiateModuleShared, getOrInstantiateRuntimeModule). Not reproducible with Webpack. Affected project: pnpm monorepo with 3 Next.js apps.

signals.topic: EPERM error blocks next build on Windows with Turbopack
signals.summary: On Windows, next build with Turbopack fails with 'EPERM: operation not permitted, open .next/trace', preventing builds from completing successfully.
signals.review_reason: Complete build failure on Windows, which is a primary development platform. The build process cannot complete, blocking deployment. Strong user impact evidence despite count=1.

source_issues.title: EPERM: operation not permitted error during next build on Windows with Next.js 15.5.14
source_issues.evidence: Build finishes but then throws uncaughtException: EPERM: operation not permitted, open '.next/trace'. Reproducible on fresh Next.js 15 project on Windows with pnpm 9.15.9. Affects the .next/trace file which is Turbopack-specific.

signals.topic: createProject API breaking change: secret env var type removed without major version bump or documentation warning
signals.summary: The vercel.projects.createProject method silently dropped support for the 'secret' type when creating environment variables, causing existing production code to fail with no deprecation notice, migration path, or documentation warning.
aliases: secret env vars no longer supported in createProject
undocumented breaking change in projects API
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed breaking change with direct user impact: reporter's production code is broken. While only 1 issue in the dataset, the nature of a silent breaking change (no major version, no deprecation notice, no docs warning) means it likely affects more users who have not yet filed reports. The root cause is clear: the 'secret' env var type was removed from createProject without proper change management, making it a genuine user pain point (workflow阻断, 主流程失败) rather than a mere feature request or roadmap item.

source_issues.title: [BREAKING CHANGE|DOC ISSUE]: vercel.projects.createProject no longer support secret vars so it breaks current code
source_issues.evidence: Reporter states a recent API change broke their product because vercel.projects.createProject no longer accepts the 'secret' type for environment variable creation, with no documentation warning or mention of the removed option.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker produces corrupted bun.lock breaking bun install --frozen-lockfile
signals.summary: turbo prune --docker generates lockfiles that fail bun install --frozen-lockfile, due to phantom npm package injection (v2.8.16) and wrong top-level version retention for removed workspaces
signals.review_reason: Two separate regressions in turbo prune --docker both cause Docker build pipelines to fail at 'bun install --frozen-lockfile' step. Issue #12262 is a confirmed v2.8.16 regression injecting ~700 phantom npm entries; issue #12504 is a separate regression with wrong top-level version retention. Both produce actionable user-blocking failures in production CI/CD pipelines. Combined count=2, each has concrete reproduction repo.

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker injects phantom npm packages into bun.lock (v2.8.16 regression from #12228)
source_issues.evidence: turbo 2.8.16 adds ~700 phantom entries (npm internals like @npmcli/*, @sigstore/*, cacache) to pruned bun.lock; bun install --frozen-lockfile correctly rejects structural mismatch

source_issues.title: turbo prune --docker keeps removed-workspace versions as top-level Bun entries, breaking bun install --frozen-lockfile
source_issues.evidence: Pruned bun.lock keeps newer top-level entries from removed frontend workspace while surviving backend graph still references older versions; bun install --frozen-lockfile fails; requires rerunning bun install to fix

signals.topic: turbo watch does not detect and re-run ^build dependency source file changes
signals.summary: turbo watch fails to watch and rebuild dependency packages that only have a build task (no dev script), breaking the 'dependency-aware' promise in docs
aliases: turbo watch dev source change rebuild
turbo watch dependency graph rebuild broken
signals.review_reason: Two issues both showing turbo watch fundamentally fails to detect source file changes in ^build dependencies. #12501 has 13 comments confirming widespread impact and explicitly calls out 'turbo watch is aware of internal dependencies' docs as contradicted. #12505 shows the watch loop is completely broken for mixed interruptible tasks. Together they show the core 'dependency-aware' watch promise is broken for shared library monorepos. This is a primary use case (incremental dev in monorepos) and is currently broken.

source_issues.title: turbo watch dev does not re-run ^build dependencies when their source files change
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed: @shared/ui#build IS in dependency graph but NOT re-run when its source files change; user must restart entire turbo watch process; affects any monorepo with shared packages using ^build; pre-2.8 versions worked correctly; 13 comments from affected users

source_issues.title: turbo watch does not restart interruptible persistent tasks on file changes
source_issues.evidence: turbo watch with mixed interruptible:true/false tasks does not react to file changes; interruptible task continues running without restart; broken in 2.9.1-canary.1

signals.topic: turbo 2.8.21+ hangs indefinitely after pulling docker compose containers, blocking dev startup
signals.summary: Regression starting in turbo 2.8.21 where docker compose up commands hang after container pull, making the dev feature completely unusable
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression: docker compose up commands that worked in 2.8.20 now hang indefinitely in 2.8.21+. This completely blocks the 'turbo dev' use case for any team running services via docker compose, which is a core monorepo dev feature. The regression is explicit (user identified last working version) and the blocking behavior is unambiguous.

source_issues.title: Turbo 2.8.20 is the last working version that starts docker compose up commands in dev script
source_issues.evidence: Turbo 2.8.20 correctly streams docker compose up output and starts/stops containers; turbo 2.8.21+ hangs after pulling containers without starting them; verified regression; last working version is explicitly identified as 2.8.20

signals.topic: affectedUsingTaskInputs flag drops ^build dependency tasks from affected task graph, causing build failures
signals.summary: When affectedUsingTaskInputs is enabled, turbo run build --affected excludes ^build dependency packages from the task graph, causing build failures in monorepos with topological dependencies
aliases: affected task graph broken topological dependencies
signals.review_reason: The affectedUsingTaskInputs future flag (meant to exclude .github/ files from triggering full rebuilds) drops the entire ^build dependency chain from the affected task graph. This causes silent build failures when the dependency's dist/ doesn't exist. While count=1, the impact is high: it makes a shipped feature flag fundamentally broken for any monorepo using ^build dependencies, and the author explicitly states 'making the feature unusable.' The root cause (match_tasks_against_changed_files() pruning transitively required dependency tasks) is clearly identified.

source_issues.title: affectedUsingTaskInputs: ^build dependencies not included for affected tasks
source_issues.evidence: When source file in @repro/web changes, turbo run build --affected only includes @repro/web#build but drops @repro/common#build (the ^build dependency); without warm cache this causes build failures because dependency's dist/ output doesn't exist; match_tasks_against_changed_files() incorrectly prunes dependency tasks; feature is unusable for any monorepo with topological dependencies

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker with npm shallow install strategy produces inconsistent package-lock.json, causing npm ci to fail with MODULE_NOT_FOUND
signals.summary: turbo prune generates package-lock.json that doesn't follow npm shallow install strategy, causing modules to be installed at wrong nesting levels and breaking postinstall scripts
aliases: turbo prune npm shallow install broken
signals.review_reason: turbo prune with npm produces package-lock.json that places packages at wrong nesting levels, causing npm ci to fail with MODULE_NOT_FOUND in the Docker prune output. This is a concrete, reproducible build pipeline failure with a minimal repro. It blocks the primary use case of turbo prune (generating self-contained Docker images). The root cause (shallow install strategy not applied to generated package-lock.json) is clearly identified.

source_issues.title: turbo prune: cannot install packages after pruning when using npm shallow install strategy
source_issues.evidence: npm ci fails in pruned repo with 'Cannot find module chalk' error; root cause is that generated package-lock.json isn't using shallow install strategy; serverless package ends up at root while chalk is in analytics-util folder; reproducible with minimal repro repo

signals.topic: CLI env commands (`env add`, `env update`) fail in CI/CD due to ignored `--yes`/`--force` flags and stdin incompatibility
signals.summary: Two separate but related CLI bugs: (1) `vercel env add <name> preview --value X --yes --force` still prompts interactively for git branch, making it unusable in GitHub Actions and other non-interactive environments. (2) `vercel env update <name> < file` (stdin redirect) fails with 'Invalid number of arguments' despite documentation saying it should work without a target. Both bugs make environment variable management impossible to automate in CI/CD pipelines.
aliases: vercel env add preview git branch prompt ignoring --yes --force
vercel env update stdin file redirect fails with Invalid number of arguments
signals.review_reason: Two related CLI bugs that both block CI/CD automation of environment variable management. Issue 15763: `--yes --force` flags are completely ignored for `env add preview`, hanging CI jobs. Issue 15764: stdin redirect is broken despite being documented as the correct usage. Combined count=2, both have clear reproducible steps and workaround paths documented.

source_issues.title: CLI: `vercel env add <name> preview` always prompts for git branch even with --yes --force
source_issues.evidence: Running `vercel env add MY_VAR preview --value 'hello' --yes --force --token=$TOKEN` still triggers interactive 'git branch' prompt, hanging CI/CD jobs. The CLI itself suggests the correct command in its error output, but that exact command still fails.

source_issues.title: CLI: `vercel env update <name> < file` fails without target, but `--value` works
source_issues.evidence: Per documentation, `vercel env update <name>` should update across all environments without target. But stdin redirect fails with 'Invalid number of arguments: vercel env update <name> <target> <gitbranch> < <file>'. Workaround is required to use `--value` instead.

signals.topic: CLI `vc link` incorrectly links to wrong project in monorepo, causing deployments to target wrong project
signals.summary: In a monorepo with similarly-named projects (e.g. `covillage-portal` and `covillage`), `vc link` consistently selects the wrong project. While `.vercel/project.json` shows correct name/id, the OIDC token is fetched for the wrong project, causing all subsequent `vc` commands to deploy to the wrong target. This completely breaks the main deployment flow for affected users.
signals.review_reason: User's main deployment flow is being redirected to the wrong project due to incorrect project resolution in `vc link`. The OIDC token mismatch means every deployment goes to the wrong target, which is a complete main-flow redirect/block for affected monorepo users. Strong evidence with screenshots and reproducible steps.

source_issues.title: CLI: I can't deploy because `vc link` keeps linking wrong project
source_issues.evidence: User has two projects 'covillage-portal' and 'covillage'; `vc link` to covillage-portal still fetches OIDC token for 'covillage', causing all `vc` deploys to target wrong project. Verified via screenshots showing mismatch between linked project name and environment variables downloaded.

signals.topic: CLI lacks `--project` flag for most commands, forcing interaction with wrong project in monorepos
signals.summary: Users with monorepos containing multiple projects cannot specify which project to target for most CLI commands. The `--project` flag works for some commands but is ignored by others, causing commands to interact with the wrong project and interfering with scripts and automation agents.
signals.review_reason: This is a structural limitation of the Vercel CLI in monorepo setups that causes the wrong project to be targeted, blocking the intended deployment workflow. While count=1, the review_reason provides strong evidence: it is a known and recurring monorepo UX issue that affects any monorepo user, not an isolated edge case.

source_issues.title: CLI Monorepo Forced Interaction
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states the CLI does not have an option to specify the project for most commands, and `--project` doesn't work for most commands. Interferes with scripts and agents. Clear feature gap in monorepo support.

signals.topic: Go `go mod vendor` projects fail to deploy: Vercel ignores vendored dependencies and runs `go mod tidy`
signals.summary: Users with Go projects that use `go mod vendor` cannot deploy on Vercel. The build process ignores vendored dependencies and runs `go mod tidy`, which fails due to private repo access. The `-mod=vendor` flag in GO_BUILD_FLAGS and environment variables are not respected by the build process. The vendor directory is present but not detected.
aliases: go mod vendor build fails vercel
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed deployment blocker for Go users with vendored dependencies. The user cannot deploy at all—the build fails and private repo access is not available. The `-mod=vendor` workaround is documented in Vercel docs but is not respected by the actual build process, making this a P1 even at count=1 due to the complete deployment阻断 nature and clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Can't get vercel to deploy a `go mod vendor`-ed project
source_issues.evidence: User has vendored Go dependencies to avoid giving Vercel access to private repos. Vercel build ignores vendor directory and runs `go mod tidy`, which fails. Setting `-mod=vendor` in GO_BUILD_FLAGS via vercel.json or UI has no effect. Proposed solution: detect vendor/modules.txt and use `-mod=vendor` automatically.

signals.topic: npm install --global vercel@latest fails with 404 for @vercel/python@6.29.0 in CI environments
signals.summary: Running `npm install --global vercel@latest` in GitHub Actions Linux runners (or any fresh Ubuntu environment) fails with NPM error 404 because the `@vercel/python@6.29.0` package is not published to npm. This blocks the initial CLI installation step in CI/CD pipelines, preventing any Vercel deployments.
aliases: vercel@latest npm install fails in CI
signals.review_reason: The issue was closed quickly (1 comment, 1 hour) suggesting it may have been a transient packaging incident rather than a persistent bug. However, the user impact is real: CI/CD pipeline fails at the CLI installation step, blocking all deployments. Confidence is lower because the issue is closed and may have been a one-time npm publish failure. Keeping with P2 because count=1 and the transient/closed nature reduces severity, though user impact in CI is clear.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: npm install --global vercel@latest fails with 404 Not Found for @vercel/python@6.29.0
source_issues.evidence: User reports: 'NPM fails to download internal package dependency resulting in a hard 404 crash' in GitHub Actions Linux runner. Error: '@vercel/python@https://registry.npmjs.org/@vercel/python/-/python-6.29.0.tgz is not in this registry'. Workaround: pin to vercel@50.37.0. Issue is closed, possibly resolved.

signals.topic: Dev container启动失败：Docker Compose配置反序列化错误
signals.summary: Zed无法解析docker compose config --format json的输出，多处YAML格式在JSON标准化后类型不匹配（labels期望数组但收到map，ports期望字符串但收到对象），导致dev container完全无法启动
aliases: docker compose config json parsing fails
docker compose labels map vs sequence
signals.review_reason: count=3且均为P1/P2级dev container核心功能阻断。3个issue覆盖了docker compose config JSON输出的3种不同反序列化失败场景（updateRemoteUserUID build阶段、port映射类型不匹配、labels数组/对象类型不匹配），根因均为docker compose --format json的标准化输出与Zed反序列化器期望格式不一致，导致dev container功能对所有使用Docker Compose的用户完全不可用，构成主流程阻断。

source_issues.title: Dev container fails with `updateRemoteUserUID` when using Docker Compose with image-only service (no features)

source_issues.title: Dev container fails to open when Docker Compose file contains `labels`
source_issues.evidence: Error deserializing from raw json: invalid type: map, expected a sequence at line 17 column 16. docker compose normalizes labels to JSON object but Zed expects array

aliases: git panel shows no branch incorrectly
git stash deletion not reflected in graph

source_issues.title: Git Panel shows "(no branch)"

signals.review_reason: 单仓count=1，但AI Agent是Zed核心差异化功能，其全面性极慢（Turtle-mode）直接损害用户购买该工具的核心价值，属于主流程体验严重退化。review_reason明确给出强用户影响证据：用户描述为'frequently'且有视频佐证，count虽为1但影响严重程度高。

source_issues.title: All agent actions extremely slow
source_issues.evidence: Text streaming, tool calls, response time, thinking blocks, code generation all extremely slow. Attached video evidence. User reports 'turtle-mode slowness has been happening frequently'. AMD Radeon 890M GPU, 62GB RAM, Linux Wayland.
